" We all had a first day of skiing here , " wrote Aspen CEO Mike Kaplan . " The mountains are open to all , and everyone on them deserves respect . " <p> The resorts contend that Ikon is n't entirely to blame for the problems . Yes , the pass attracted more skiers than expected , says Anna Cole , communications manager at Jackson Hole , but the larger number of skiers merely highlighted existing pinch points . " I think what we learned this year -- and we 're still learning and will be analysing all this data -- is that there are more improvements to be made to our infrastructure , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ snow and record-breaking visitation . " <p> Jackson Hole estimated that only 8% of its attendees this season have been first-timers brought by Ikon ( Pic : Bloomberg ) <p> Jeff Hanle , director of public relations for Aspen Skiing Co , argues that the sheer amount of snow was primarily responsible for the huge turnouts , especially since so many storm cycles lined up with weekends . " This is a benchmark year , a once-a-decade sort of season , " says Bill Jensen , a 45-year ski industry veteran and CEO of Telluride , which estimates that 8% of its skiers this year utilised the Epic Pass . <p> Backlash aside , Ikon 's arrival has been great for powder chasers . Mega-passes offer skiers greater choice than ever , at far lower prices -- explaining why , of the estimated 9.2 million skiers and snowboarders in the US , well over one million bought either Ikon or Epic passes this year . <p> That popularity has made them essential for mountains , too . " We want a thriving economy without falling into that old ski town trap of not wanting others to come after we 've arrived @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ new CEO , agreed in an opinion piece of her own . " If Jackson Hole had chosen not to participate in one of those passes , skier visits might have dropped to levels at which we could not sustain our operations , " she wrote . <p> To many locals , the argument rang hollow . " This is an unbelievable falsehood , " wrote @Ikonoftheday in a caption below a screenshot of Buckley 's statement . " ( T ) he truth is that JHM ( Jackson Hole Mountain ) is uniquely capable of surviving as a standalone resort , but the powers that be apparently do not want it to . " <p> Mountain managers are taking steps to make Ikon work for everyone . Some of those steps , such as cutting marketing and promotional efforts late in the season , after most sales have taken place , seem more like stumbles . But every resort says it has learned from this year 's experience . Jackson Hole has made transportation and parking priorities , partnering with Teton County and the Teton Village Association to invest @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ on snow and the fickle skiers that follow it , big capital expenditures can be tricky . <p> " The biggest question looking forward is : What is the snow going to do ? " says Forsell . " As we learn and grow , we 're focused on how do we tweak and craft this product to keep it positive . " <p> One way to keep it positive is to turn local critics into converts . But given the convenience and the chance to chase snow at other mountains , many local skiers are likely to end up gritting their teeth as they realise they 've become Ikon skiers . -- Bloomberg

@@40887621 <h> Role of forwarding agency in handling of cargo <p> WE refer to the reports headlined " China 's ban , Malaysia 's bane " and " When trash is cash " ( The Star , April 24 ) . In the second report , it is stated that 111 containers of contaminated plastic waste unfit for recycling at Westports and 18 containers at Northport were still unclaimed . <p> Selangor Freight Forwarders and Logistics Association , the largest association in Selangor representing the forwarding industry , wishes to comment on these reports . Our association and the Federation of Malaysian Freight Forwarders ( national association ) fully support the government 's initiative to stop the illegal import of plastic waste into this country . In fact , we gave our full support when this issue was brought up by a member of the Council of Eminent Persons ( CEP ) during our session with them in June last year . Our associations maintain our commitment and support for the government 's initiative on banning the import of unrecyclable plastic waste . <p> The above report quoted Energy , Science , Technology , Environment and Climate Change Minister Yeo @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ clients importing plastics , adding that the government had the right to revoke the agencies ' licences if their clients made false customs declaration " . <p> We wish to advise that forwarding agencies are only intermediaries acting on behalf of importers and exporters to bring in or ship out goods . Any information declared by the forwarding agencies are given by the importer or exporter or obtained from the bill of lading ( BL ) or manifest provided by the shipping lines . The forwarding agent is not present when the cargo is loaded at the point of origin and does not know who the shipper is until he is engaged by the importer to declare the customs form . <p> Shipping lines have access to information about the shipper and cargo . This information is in the BL and shipping manifest . In some countries , for example those in the European Union , the Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System ( HS code ) of the cargo is required in the BL and manifest . The forwarding agency is only given the information by the importer through @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to declare the customs form on behalf of customers . <p> Hence , forwarding agents are in no position to verify the information provided to them by the importer or the shipping lines , contrary to the allegation of collusion between forwarding agencies and their clients as reported . <p> Where no HS code is provided , the forwarding agency may propose for one to be declared to customs based on the cargo description given by the importer . However , customs may amend or change the tariff code or require examination of the cargo before determining the correct HS code . Thus , a forwarding agent declares the goods based only on the information he gets , and he is in no position to verify the accuracy of the information . <p> The report also says " The forwarding companies , she said , had the right to open up the containers should they have suspicions about the contents . " We wish to clarify that pending release by customs or any relevant government agency , the forwarding agent has no right to open the container . If he @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ customs , he would have to get approval from the shipping line and customs , as the procedure involves the liability of the shipping line . The liability might be affected as most containers are on a " shipper load and count basis " , and if the seal is broken or opened without the required approval , the shipping line would not accept any responsibility . Customs would also have queries if a container is opened and its seal does not tally with the original seal number that was declared . <p> While it is still possible for a forwarding agent to open a container , he would have little information other than that provided to him by the importer to arouse his suspicion to get the said container opened . <p> The report also says " They are falsely declaring it as ( HS Code ) 3920 , which does n't need a permit and can enter the country ... " Our comment is that if this HS code is declared , customs or the relevant agency could request for the container to be examined . <p> As @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the approvals were given for export and declared by the exporter to their respective customs and environment departments , and the shipping lines accepting this cargo know what they are carrying . So we need to go back to the source and hold shipping lines and exporters accountable for this issue . <p> The shipping line involved should take the cargo back and return it to the known exporter . <p> This action should be taken by our authority as this is what Thailand and Vietnam are doing under the Basel Convention . Please go to the source to eradicate the waste exporter syndicates . <p> We also fully support the minister 's decision for our representatives attending the Conference of the Parties to the Basel Convention to seek " international cooperation to take down these global syndicates " . We also suggest that the government 's representatives at the conference propose that all the shippers be made responsible for shipping back cargoes of unrecyclable plastic waste to their countries of origin . <p> At home , the government could direct all the importers to send the cargoes back to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ punishment . <p> The Selangor Freight Forwarders and Logistics Association does not support any forwarding agency that intentionally colludes or conspires with or abets anyone to falsely declare the import of unrecyclable plastic waste into our country . If any forwarding agency runs foul of the law , it should be brought to book and handed penalties that go beyond revoking its licence . <p> We hope our comments have clarified the position of forwarding agencies and that our members would not be tarred with the same brush as smugglers .

send the much needed adrenalin to oil producers and pulling many O&amp;G players out of the doldrums <p> by MARK RAO / pic by MUHD AMIN NAHARUL <p> THE bulls have stormed the oil market as tightening supply and production disruptions coupled with renewed demand prospects have sent crude oil prices to six-month highs . <p> Brent oil rallied approximately 37% this year alone to above US$74 ( RM303.40 ) per barrel , sending the much needed adrenalin to oil producers like Malaysia and pulling many oil and gas ( O&amp;G ) players out of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ rout , O&amp;G firms capitalised on the high crude prices of above US$100 per barrel to expand , raising billions to finance more projects . <p> The subsequent rout which saw oil prices plunging 57.5% in just six months from June 2014 to January a year later , had trimmed spendings from major producers , leaving O&amp;G companies saddled with billions of debts . <p> The prospects for the oil sector have improved significantly on OPEC-led production cuts and further bolstered by oil disruptions at a few major producers . <p> SPI Asset Management managing partner and head of trading Stephen Innes said there is a " technical overhang " from overextended bullish bets on both Brent and West Texas Intermediate oil contracts . <p> " Any breakdown on the technical or fundamental landscape can trigger a reasonably aggressive market response as weaker longs head for the exits , " he said in a research note last Friday . <p> While the Chinese economy -- the world 's second-largest oil consumer -- is showing signs of stabilising , the dovishness of central banks worldwide are indicating that the global economy @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ recession fears have largely been ruled out and presently there is sufficient support from the supply side of the market for crude oil to make further strides towards the US$80 per barrel mark in 2019 . <p> The Malaysian Reserve looks at benefactors from the higher oil prices and companies , which shiver with every US$1 increase of the commodity . <p> Govt Coffers Versus Consumer Pressures <p> The Malaysian government based its 2019 budget on an average Brent of US$70 per barrel for the year . <p> Crude oil only surpassed this threshold earlier this month , but it is estimated that the government will gain RM300 million in additional revenue for every US$1 increase above the US$70 per barrel average . <p> While the inverse also holds true , the additional income is a welcome relief to the current government who is working towards paring down its over RM1 trillion in debt . <p> Higher oil prices also bodes well for the ringgit , which performance is generally correlated to the movement of the commodity . The local unit remains bogged down by external risks , but such @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ The ringgit is expected to be on a stronger footing this year . <p> While high oil prices benefit the government , its subsidies for fuel will also rise in tandem . Any removal of the subsidies would impact the consumers at the pump and increase inflation . <p> Currently , retail fuel prices are determined by a weekly float mechanism with RON95 and diesel capped at RM2.08 and RM2.18 per litre respectively . <p> The system was introduced early in January this year . But , it could make way for a targeted petrol subsidy mechanism which could see the cap lifted for RON95 . <p> Petronas ' Gain , Airlines ' Pain <p> The 2014-2015 oil crisis taught national oil companies a proverbial lesson : The need to be lean in managing cost , while avoiding exuberant spending amid a market that swings to a downturn as easily as it goes on a bull run . <p> Petroliam Nasional Bhd ( Petronas ) had emerged stronger and leaner from the 2014 oil rout and providing RM19 billion in impairments in 2015 , eroding its profits that year . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ spending and trimmed some 1,000 staff in 2016 . <p> The leaner base allowed Petronas to announce its highest profit since 2013 when it grew its profit after tax by 22% year-on-year ( YoY ) to RM55.3 billion last year as revenue rose 12% to RM251 billion . <p> This allowed the company to allocate a higher upstream spend of RM30 billion in 2019 -- half of which will be spent domestically . But , Petronas continues with a conservative outlook for the year with projects budgeted at a Brent of US$66 per barrel . <p> Crude oil trending above US$70 per barrel bodes well for the company 's upstream business , which is the main revenue generator of the state-owned company . <p> The higher margins will also help the company to meet its dividend commitments to the government -- its sole shareholder -- which totals RM54 billion in respect to its 2018 fiscal year . <p> Listed AirAsia and AirAsia X recognised RM394.97 million and RM99.27 million in losses respectively , for the quarter ended Dec 31 last year on higher fuel and other expenses . <p> Airlines @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ on the additional cost to passengers to protect their bottom line . However , this was historically done during peak oil price levels of above US$100 per barrel . <p> At about US$74 per barrel today , Malaysian airline operators are expected to bear the additional costs rather than risk deterring passenger traffic due to higher fares . <p> The O&amp;G Value Chain <p> The bulk of listed O&amp;G companies in Malaysia are service providers who are engaged in the upstream sector and are predominantly dependent on Petronas for work . <p> This includes companies such as Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd , Uzma Bhd and Velesto Energy Bhd , while Sapura Energy Bhd and Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd have an international base to support their domestic business . <p> Petronas upping its upstream expenditure to RM30 billion , coupled with a brighter activity outlook over the next three years , bodes well for local O&amp;G service providers as a whole . <p> The company foresees higher activities and demand for drilling , marine and maintenance works from 2019 to 2021 with double the capacity needed for jack-up rigs . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ such as Velesto who recently secured RM432.33 million worth of contracts from Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd -- Petronas ' upstream vehicle -- for jack-up drilling rig services . <p> " The contracts will translate into better utilisation for Velesto 's assets , while service providers such as Dayang are expected to see higher work orders this year , " said the industry analyst . <p> Meanwhile , global upstream activity will be supported by the development of new fields , particularly in the Middle East where the majority of the final investment decisions will be concentrated in , the source added . <p> " This will benefit companies with larger international exposures such as Sapura Energy and Serba Dinamik , " said the analyst . <p> Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd and Reach Energy Bhd are also set to profit with the current rise as they have a direct leverage on oil prices as pure-play exploration and production ( E&amp;P ) players .

Tuesday , April 30th , 2019 at , News <p> by AFIQ AZIZ / pic by BERNAMA <p> In 2008 , food prices spiked to unprecedented levels , sending shivers throughout the globe -- especially in the poor and underdeveloped countries . Prices of grains rose multifold , putting the world on a brink of another food crisis last witnessed in 1973 to 1975 . <p> According to figures , the cereal price index reached a peak of 2.8 times higher in 2008 compared to 2000 . Prices of food commodities @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the roof as the world also witnessed the global financial crisis unfolding in developed countries . <p> As rice , corn , wheat and soybeans were the staple food for billions of people and accounted for a substantial amount of expenditures among the poor , the food crisis of 2008 triggered riots , social tensions and unrests in over 30 countries , especially in poor and underdeveloped nations . <p> It was estimated that about 150 million of people were left on the brink of hunger . Rice , which is the staple food for billions of people in Asia , was not spared from the crisis . <p> The price of rice jumped to about US$1,000 ( RM4,130 ) a tonne in May 2008 compared to about US$220 in early 2004 , more than a 450% increase . <p> Countries in Asia were the main producers of rice , however , they too struggled to ensure sufficient supplies for their people . Rice export restrictions were imposed to protect supplies to domestic markets . <p> The move further fuelled the price hike of rice . Food-importing countries scrambled to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ like India and Vietnam had banned exports . Panic-buying by countries like the Philippines , one of the world 's largest rice importers , had exacerbated the situation , driving the price higher . <p> Panic swept across Asia after the dire situation in the Philippines and consumers scrambled to empty shelves and stocks at rice retailers in many countries . <p> But a majority of Malaysians did not realise that the world was facing a food crisis . <p> " Malaysians just went to any shop and continued to purchase rice at a subsidised price . They did n't even realise that there was a food crisis and rice shortage globally , " said an industry insider . <p> Malaysia is among the few countries that had circumvented the full impact of the price hike and supply shortage , despite it was an importer of the staple food . Consumers were paying no more than RM3 for 1kg of rice , although the price of the staple food had tripled . <p> The " Single Gatekeeping Mechanism " ( SGM ) , which has Padiberas Nasional Bhd ( Bernas @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , prevented the food crisis in Malaysia . <p> According to reports , the rice concession company incurred losses of more than RM70 million during the 20082009 crisis due to higher import prices , while keeping transacted prices at the lower end . <p> Bernas was the evolution of Lembaga Padi dan Beras Negara ( LPN ) which was established in 1971 . <p> The setting up of LPN was to ensure the availability of rice at an affordable price and guarantee the wellbeing of farmers . There are almost 200,000 local farmers who depend on the crop for their livelihood . <p> LPN was given the sole right to manage the country 's rice supply after the 1973 rice crisis . The crisis which was triggered by a large-scale El Nino event sharply reduced the dry season crop throughout South-East Asia , especially in Indonesia , Thailand and the Philippines . <p> Thailand , the world 's leading rice exporter , at that time banned rice export altogether , triggering a panic across the region . <p> On the other hand , local rice importers declined to import the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ rice shortage in the country . <p> Following the incident , the government entrusted LPN to be the sole guardian of the country 's rice sector . <p> In return , LPN must ensure that the farmer 's wellbeing is taken care of , the prices of imported rice are not lower than local rice and ensure market stability . <p> Under the SGM , Bernas will have to import rice regardless of international price volatility and complement the shortage of local production which is short by 30% to 40% . <p> Bernas today plays many roles in the post-harvest chain from the procurement and processing of paddy , importation , warehousing , and to the distribution and marketing of rice in Malaysia . <p> It is also the buyer of last resort ( BOLR ) where the company has no choice but to purchase paddy irrespective of the quality at a guaranteed price . <p> A recent research report warned about the implications of liberalising the import of rice in a fragile midstream ecosystem , the absence of a social net to help paddy growers and the ramifications to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Khazanah Research Institute ( KRI ) titled " The Status of the Paddy and Rice Industry in Malaysia " , Malaysia consumed 80kg of rice per person in 2016 , which is about 26% of the total caloric intake per day , costing an average of RM44/month per household . <p> Households in Sabah spent the most on rice at RM73/ month , while households in Perlis spent the least at just RM13/month , the report said . <p> The report said Malaysians consumed 2.7 million metric tonnes of rice , whereby 67% was produced locally and the rest imported primarily from Thailand , Vietnam and Pakistan . <p> In the last few months , Bernas ' monopoly of the rice and paddy sector has been under scrutiny . There are suggestions that the government should abolish monopolies in Malaysia , including Bernas ' role as the caretaker of the country 's rice imports . <p> Bernas denied the claims , saying that it has both national and social responsibilities to ensure prices are kept low and the produce of 200,000 paddy growers are protected under the BOLR . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ any excess of paddy produced under the BOLR at the guaranteed minimum price of RM1,200 per tonne . <p> Bernas operates 28 mills from a total of about 180 mills across the country , with purchases of over 500,000 tonnes of local harvest including under the BOLR . The other 152 private mills purchase around 1.2 million tonnes of yields , largely quality grain . <p> Agriculture and Agrobased Industry Minister Datuk Salahuddin Ayub said the government will try to convince Bernas to accept its " soft landing " proposal by appointing a few rice importers before 2021 . <p> However , the viability of the new system in safeguarding the Malaysian staple food is still unclear . Salahuddin is also mulling the re-establishment of LPN , where all the industry stakeholders will be put under one umbrella . <p> Based on the LPN financial report , on average , the government subsidised the body around RM54.8 million per annum or a total of RM1.26 billion from 1972 to 1994 . <p> It is not known if the government will be willing to spend the millions of ringgit to form @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ already subsidised to the tune of about RM1.7 billion in 2017 and any additional expenses will weigh on the government 's already thin budget . <p> There are also arguments that surrendering the SGM will open the country 's risk to a food security issue again , similar to the event in the 1970s where importers declined to import the grain in the event of high prices . <p> " It somehow would be challenging for the government to strike a balance between the 200,000 rice growers ' wellbeing , while maintaining the low prices of rice and its availability across the state in the country , " said an industry player . <p> The KRI report also suggested that a high market share does not automatically constitute a monopoly or abuse of dominant power . <p> " Bernas does not have the power to set the prices for rice , which are determined by the government through ceiling prices , " said the research institute . @@40899014 <p> * Affin Bank 's net interest margin to come under pressure from NSFR requirements ; looks to higher yielding assets to mitigate the decline * Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd ( PetChem ) has allocated a capex of up to RM2.7bil for 2019 , of which about RM500mil will be used for turnaround activities at six of its plants : chairman Datuk Md Arif Mahmood * Malaysia will be exhibiting sustainable energy solutions at the Expo 2020 Dubai ; expects to secure RM10b of investments : Energy , Technology , Science , Climate Change and Environment Minister Yeo Bee Yin <p> China likes to tout the virtues of its private sector , whose firms are the source of most new jobs and most economic growth in the country . Not all private companies are created equal , however . Those perceived to have the state 's backing can grow disturbingly fast and crash to earth just as quickly . <p> Behemoth China Minsheng Investment Group Corp ( CMIG ) is only the latest example . The company was founded in May 2014 to act as a private sector version of a sovereign wealth fund , one that would supposedly @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ founding investors included 59 different private companies , who pooled together some 40 billion yuan ( RM24 billion ) in registered capital . <p> As of last September , the most recent financial data available , the group was carrying 232 billion yuan in debt , 63% of it due within a year . As with other fast-growing private conglomerates such as HNA Group Co Ltd and energy trader CEFC China Energy Co Ltd , those obligations have started to unravel . CMIG has tested bondholders ' nerves repeatedly this year with late repayments , the latest of which spread offshore and triggered cross-default clauses on dollar bonds that had been worth US$800 million ( RM3.28 billion ) . <p> CMIG 's stunning growth has inevitably created the impression that the firm has political backing . It openly describes itself as the brainchild of Premier Li Keqiang . In a 2016 bond prospectus , the group noted it was " the only private enterprise approved by the State Council to use ' China ' in its name " and that it regarded " serving ( China 's ) national strategy @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ spend US$5 billion developing an industrial park in Indonesia as part of President Xi Jinping 's signature Belt and Road infrastructure-building programme , and talked up investing in Vietnam and Cambodia . <p> Within two years of its founding , the company had won credit lines with policy banks such as China Development Bank and Export- Import Bank of China , the latter now mired in an asset-disposal dispute with the firm . CMIG enjoyed about US$10 billion in loan facilities from the two policy banks and China 's big four commercial banks -- an unusually large amount for such a young private company . <p> There 's nothing inherently wrong with relatively easy credit . But it can breed overconfidence , leading firms to take on riskier long-term projects . <p> When that tap closes all of a sudden , as it frequently can in China , companies such as CMIG can be stuck with illiquid projects desperate for cash injections . <p> For instance , shortly after its founding , CMIG spent 25 billion yuan , or roughly two-thirds of its capital raise , on a prime plot @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ best investment -- Shanghai 's property price has soared since -- but the deal did n't work out : CMIG had promised to develop the plot by 2020 , which meant it required the kind of cash the now-distressed company no longer has . The property was sold under pressure to state-owned developer Greenland Holdings Group Co Ltd to honour a February bond repayment . <p> CMIG could face similar problems elsewhere in its portfolio . In late 2016 , in a US$2.6 billion deal , CMIG took control of Yida China Holdings Ltd , which specialises in property developments in lower-tier cities such as Dalian . China 's smaller cities have a notorious oversupply issue , and sure enough , sales at Yida have been stagnant in the last three years , while those of its larger competitors have rebounded . <p> And then there 's CMIG 's unfortunate venture into solar energy , which followed the meteoric rise of Hanergy Thin Film Power Group Ltd . In 2015 , CMIG sought to build the world 's largest solar park . By last June , it had plowed over @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ for their long investment cycles . ( CMIG 's biggest project in the Ningxia province wo n't break even for nearly a decade , even using the company 's own aggressive assumptions . ) <p> Meanwhile , the policy tide is turning . Tired of hefty subsidy bills , Beijing now only welcomes solar parks to supply to its grids if they do n't require government aid . <p> While CMIG continues to tout the potential of Belt and Road investments , prospects are dwindling there , too , in part because of a backlash among recipient countries . Its construction work at Country Garden Holdings Co Ltd 's US$100 billion Forest City project in Malaysia has stalled ever since Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad balked at foreigners buying property there . Its Indonesian industrial park has gone nowhere . <p> The Belt and Road label does have one key advantage : CMIG can be kept alive longer if it can show it owns strategic assets . Nearly a year since it first defaulted , energy trader CEFC has yet to be put into a bankruptcy process in China @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to offload its minority stake in an Abu Dhabi oil concession -- a strategically important asset -- before its other assets fall into creditors ' hands . <p> CMIG has n't grown big enough to pose a systemic financial risk . Still , China should be wary of allowing such private sector giants to swell largely on perceptions of political support . Sooner or later , those bills will come due . -- Bloomberg <p> This column does not necessarily reflect the opinion of the editorial board or Bloomberg LP and its owners .

@@40900333 <h> Putting the ' radioactivity ' of Lynas waste in perspective <p> LETTER With the ongoing discussion regarding the Lynas Corporation plant , there needs to be a clarification of the levels of radioactivity that are being discussed and what they mean . <p> The Lynas plant has met all conditions for safe operation over the past six years . It has been subject to a parliamentary review committee , two reports by the International Atomic Energy Agency ( IAEA ) , and the most recent December 2018 review committee report . Various court actions by opponents in the past have all failed . <p> Despite this technical and regulatory-based history of safe and compliant operation , there was an almost simultaneous press release by Energy , Science , Technology , Environment and Climate Change Minister Yeo Bee Yin in December 2018 of her intention to force Lynas to send the water leach purification residue ( WLP ) back to Australia , contrary to the review committee report . <p> This furore is all based on some peoples ' perception of very low levels of radioactivity still being ' radioactive ' , and they think dangerously so . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ perspective . The levels of radioactivity in the concentrate coming from Australia and the WLP produced at the Lynas Advanced Materials Plant ( Lamp ) are similar at about 6 Bq/g of thorium-232 . A Bq , or Becquerel , is one atom decaying per second . That is a very small unit , being at the individual atom scale . <p> This level of activity is described by the IAEA as very low and intrinsically low risk . It does not require placarding as radioactive for transport or processing internationally and in other countries because it is below the 10 Bq/g level above which that would be required . Malaysia historically happens to use a low 1 Bq/g limit based on an old out-dated standard . <p> It is worth noting here that there is radioactivity in all environments . We all receive radiation from the ground , the structures we live and work in , the food we consume , from space ( cosmic radiation ) and from each other ( there is about 7,000-8,000 Bq in the average 70kg human body ) . <p> Additionally , there @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ on much higher levels of radiation from the earth than average , from thorium . <p> Studies have found that there have been no noticeable deleterious health effects over many years . Examples of such places are Ramsar in Iran , Guarapari in Brazil , Karunagappally in India , and Yangjiang in China . <p> These high background areas are caused by thermal springs , radioactive sands and rocks and such materials used in building products , or a combination of these . <p> For comparison , the concentration of radioactivity in WLP to that in the human body is about the same ratio of the radiation that everyone receives when flying at greater than 10,000m altitude compared to that at ground level . <p> So , whenever you see Yeo , Bentong MP Wong Tack , Kuantan MP Fuziah Salleh or anti-Lynas protestors taking commercial flights you should realise the extent of their hypocrisy in accepting definite higher levels of radiation at altitude . <p> That is while they are continuing their non-scientific , irrational claims of dangerous radioactivity in a material that no other jurisdiction would deem to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the radioactivity in other by-products that are produced in Malaysia , or indeed , imported , such as phosphate fertilisers . <p> But then Lynas ' critics would say the thorium is long-lived with a half-life of 14 billion years . Let 's look more closely at the radioactivity in the human body . It is dominated by potassium-40 , which is 0.0117 percent of all the potassium in the world . <p> Since potassium is an essential ingredient in our bodies , we contain a small mass of this radioactive nuclide . The typical body will have around 4500 Bq of Potassium-40 , and , yes , potassium-40 is a long-lived nuclide with a half-life of 1.3 billion years . <p> The three politicians or associates may then also claim that " secular equilibrium " means that the activity in the WLP is actually higher due to the decay products from the thorium-232 . <p> During the processing that " secular equilibrium " has been destroyed and it takes decades to re-establish for thorium-232 . And the accepted international standard is based on thorium-232 taking into account the various @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to highlight the relativities of these levels of radioactivity and the scaremongering by those opposing Lynas for whatever ulterior motives . <p> As proven and stated , the levels of radioactivity in concentrate and WLP are very low and intrinsically low risk . <p> Other naturally occurring radioactive materials are frequently used and utilised around the world in many applications , and are not subject to such stringent restrictions or requirements that a vocal minority of people are trying to implement ( selectively ) to one particular company in Malaysia . <p> The views expressed here are those of the author/contributor and do not necessarily represent the views of Malaysiakini.
